question: After wildfire in boreal forests, what controls natural conifer regeneration (fire interval, fire severity, seed supply, seedbed type), and which conditions signal that regeneration will fail without active restoration?

edges.subject: Short-interval fire history
edges.object: Decreased total black spruce seed rain
edges.sentence: Total (X<sup>2</sup> = 87.00, df = 2, p < 0.001) and viable (X<sup>2</sup> = 13.35, df = 2, p = 0.001) black spruce seed rain counts differed significantly among fire history classes (Table 1). This difference was due to SI sites, which had lower counts of both total (z = -8.83, p < 0.001) and viable (z = -4.73, p < 0.001) black spruce seed than MF and LI sites

edges.subject: Presence of dense fireweed thickets
edges.sentence: Observations from field tours conducted in the summer of 1992 indicated that survival and growth on subalpine c1earcuts is particularly poor under thickets of dense fireweed.

edges.subject: logging in TB408
edges.object: failure of natural regeneration of white spruce
edges.sentence: Failure of post-logging natural regeneration in Wood Buffalo National Park is attributable primarily to two factors: (1) large size of the clearcuts, placing most of any area logged beyond the effective dispersal distance of white spruce seed; (2) destruction of advance growth (seedlings and transgressives) and lack of residual growth (trees and saplings).

edges.subject: Long-interval fire history
edges.object: Increased presence of black spruce seedlings
edges.sentence: The binomial model, which was built upon presence/absence data, indicated that LI sites had significantly more plots with black spruce seedlings present than SI or MF sites, and black spruce seedlings were significantly more abundant in hollows than on hummocks.

edges.object: Mean percent viability of black spruce seeds
edges.sentence: The mean percent viability did not differ in MF, LI, and SI sites (8.0 ± 1.5%, 6.5 ± 0.9%, and 7.2 ± 4.8%, respectively; F = 0.066, df = 2, p = 0.93).
